questions.stem: A notebook fails with an error that a column can't be resolved. The column exists in the source file. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The name in the code doesn't match the DataFrame's schema, for example different spelling or a column lost in an earlier select
The Spark pool is too small
The lakehouse is in a different domain

questions.explanation: An unresolved column error means the plan refers to a column the DataFrame doesn't have at that point. Print the schema before the failing step.

questions.stem: A notebook fails with an out-of-memory error on the driver at df.toPandas() on a large table. What is the best fix?

options.text: Aggregate or filter in Spark first, and bring only the small result to the driver

questions.explanation: toPandas and collect pull all the data onto the driver. Keep the work distributed in Spark and only bring small results back.

questions.stem: A notebook fails with ModuleNotFoundError for a package it imports. The package must be available to every run, including scheduled ones. What should you do?

options.text: Add the package to an environment and attach the environment to the notebook or workspace

questions.explanation: An environment's libraries are installed in every session that uses it, including scheduled runs. An in-session install lasts only for that session.

questions.stem: Two notebooks append to and update the same Delta table at once, and one fails with a concurrent modification conflict. Which approach helps?

options.text: Retry the failed write, or make the jobs write to separate partitions so they don't conflict

questions.explanation: Delta uses optimistic concurrency: conflicting commits fail and can be retried, and writers that touch separate partitions conflict far less.
